title: BETWEEN Operator
description: Learn how to use the BETWEEN operator to test if a value falls within a specified range of values.

data.text: The BETWEEN operator is a logical operator that allows you to specify a range to test.

data.title: BETWEEN Syntax
data.content: Test if a value falls within an inclusive range.
data.code: column | expression BETWEEN start_expression AND end_expression

items: Specify the column or expression to test.
Place the start_expression and end_expression between the BETWEEN and the AND keywords.
The start_expression, end_expression, and the expression to test must have the same data type.

data.text: The BETWEEN operator returns TRUE if the expression to test is greater than or equal to the start_expression and less than or equal to the end_expression.
You can substitute the BETWEEN operator with the >= and <= comparison operators combined with AND:

data.title: BETWEEN vs Comparison Operators
data.content: BETWEEN is more readable than >= AND <=.
data.code: column | expression <= end_expression AND column | expression >= start_expression

data.text: To negate the result of the BETWEEN operator, use the NOT BETWEEN operator:

data.title: NOT BETWEEN Syntax
data.content: Negate the BETWEEN result to find values outside the range.
data.code: column | expression NOT BETWEEN start_expression AND end_expression

data.title: NULL Handling
data.text: If any input to the BETWEEN or NOT BETWEEN operator is NULL, the result is UNKNOWN.

data.title: BETWEEN with Numbers
data.content: Find products with list prices between 149.99 and 199.99.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price BETWEEN 149.99 AND 199.99
ORDER BY
    list_price;

data.title: NOT BETWEEN with Numbers
data.content: Find products with list prices outside the 149.99-199.99 range.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price NOT BETWEEN 149.99 AND 199.99
ORDER BY
    list_price;

data.title: BETWEEN with Dates
data.content: Find orders placed between January 15 and January 17, 2017.
data.code:
SELECT
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    order_date,
    order_status
FROM
    sales.orders
WHERE
    order_date BETWEEN '20170115' AND '20170117'
ORDER BY
    order_date;

data.title: Date Format
data.text: To specify a literal date, use the format YYYYMMDD where YYYY is a 4-digit year, MM is a 2-digit month, and DD is a 2-digit day.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The BETWEEN operator tests if a value falls within an inclusive range.
BETWEEN is equivalent to >= and <= combined with AND.
Use NOT BETWEEN to find values outside a range.
BETWEEN is more readable than comparison operators for range tests.
If any input to BETWEEN is NULL, the result is UNKNOWN.
